Initial state in equilibrium with an observed flow

Source: R/initial_flow.R
initial_state_from_flow.Rd

A warm start that replaces an arbitrary soil fraction with a state consistent with the flow observed at the start of the run. It assumes the catchment is in a steady state at that moment, as it approximately is in a dry-weather recession:

Usage

initial_state_from_flow(
  model,
  observed_m3s,
  baseflow_fraction,
  soil_fraction = 0.5
)

Arguments

model

A FlodePdmModel.

observed_m3s

Observed flow at the start of the run, m3/s; finite and at least qc.

baseflow_fraction

Share of the natural flow that is baseflow, in [0, 1].

soil_fraction

Soil storage as a fraction of capacity, used only with split recharge, in [0, 1].

Value

A validated FlodePdmState with step 0.

Details

  • natural flow is observed_m3s minus qc, converted to mm/h, and divided into baseflow (baseflow_fraction) and surface flow (the rest);

  • each routing store, or both stores of a cascade, is set to deliver its share in equilibrium, using storage_for_flow();

  • the soil store is set so that recharge equals baseflow. With standard recharge this is S = st + (kg * qb)^(1 / bg); with demand recharge it is the soil storage at which the demand formula gives qb. With split recharge the soil store does not drain to groundwater, so the steady state does not determine it and soil_fraction of capacity is used. The soil store is capped at capacity;

  • the outlet delay queues hold the water already in transit at that flow.

The state's instantaneous flow then equals observed_m3s. The first simulated interval is a mean over the interval, so it departs from the observation as the stores respond to the forcing; with no rain the surface store recedes.

baseflow_fraction has no default: it varies widely between catchments. For UK gauged catchments the baseflow index (BFI) published by the National River Flow Archive is a reasonable value. An exponential store has no steady state at zero flow, so its share of the flow must be positive.

The compiled core does the same calculation (pdm_state_from_flow() in src/pdm_core.h).

References

Moore (2007), doi:10.5194/hess-11-483-2007.

Examples

model <- pdm_model(area_km2 = 44)
state <- initial_state_from_flow(model, observed_m3s = 0.8, baseflow_fraction = 0.6)
run_pdm(model, data.frame(rain = c(0, 0), pet = c(0, 0)), state)$output$q_m3s
#> [1] 0.7944496 0.7681147
